assign.request: patterns - what emerged from 47 websites: the most common layouts, and the best. A page at /websites/patterns/ whose every number is computed live from site/index.json, plus judgments in prose beside it.
steps: count live in Node: layouts by width, sections, tags, collapse transitions
look at shots for the best-of-category judgments
register: websites children, front link, layouts link
shoot 400 and 1920, zero console errors, numbers agree

log.msg: Counted live over site/index.json (47 sites). At 1920: 2-sidebar 14, 1-bands 10, 1-centered 8, 3-holy-grail 7, 1-flow 3, 4-1 2, 2-equal 2, 3-cards 1. By column count at 1920: one column 21, two 16, three 8, four 2. At 400: 1-flow 38, 1-bands 7, 2-sidebar 1 (amazon-kindle-product), 4-1 1 (nike-home) - so all but 9 are 1-flow, and all but 2 are down to a single column.

Collapse 1920->400: 2-sidebar->1-flow 14, 1-centered->1-flow 8, 1-bands->1-bands 7, 3-holy-grail->1-flow 6, 1-bands->1-flow 3, 1-flow->1-flow 3, 2-equal->1-flow 2, 3-holy-grail->2-sidebar 1, 4-1->1-flow 1, 3-cards->1-flow 1, 4-1->4-1 1. Only two transitions keep more than one column at 400.

Section layouts (index.sections): 1-flow 47, 2-sidebar 19, 2-equal 16, n-wall 12, 1-centered 11, 3-equal 7, 3-holy-grail 7, 4-equal 7, 3-cards 2, 4-1 2. n-wall appears only as a SECTION, never as a whole page - the corpus has no page-level n-wall.

DECISION: the judgments live one click down at /websites/patterns/best/, written as public/websites/patterns/best.md. core/Page renders a .md beside a page at that name (Page.class.js: a .md file beside me IS a page), so the child needs no page.js of its own - fewest moving parts, and level 1 stays one screen as the newcomer rule demands. A second section below the fold would have doubled the front page.

DECISION: the corpus spells the documentation category three ways - documentation (5), docs (2), reference (1). The page counts categories literally, as written; the judgments merge the three into one documentation verdict and say so. Cannot fix the records: the fence forbids writing a site record.

links.label: The best of each kind - the judgments

log.msg: PROOF. Rendered headline, read out of the live DOM: "Of 47 real websites, 21 are one column at 1920, 16 are two, 8 are three and 2 are four. At 400 all but 9 are 1-flow - one column, each row the full width - and 7 of those 9 are still a single column, so only 2 of the 47 keep a second column on a phone." My own Node count over site/index.json: 1-* 21, 2-* 16, 3-* 8, 4-* 2 at 1920; 47-38=9 not 1-flow at 400, 7 of them 1-bands, 2 with more than one column. They agree exactly.

Verified headless at 400 and 1920 (and 1920x2400 for the lower half): zero console errors, zero 4xx responses, no horizontal overflow, no framed box at x:0, no unwanted scrollers. /websites/patterns/best/ is clean too, all 8 inline shots load, all 42 links in best.md resolve against layouts.json and site/index.json. Shots in this dir.

Two defects found and fixed while looking. (1) The alias arrow fired on TAGS as well as ids, so the tag panel read "measure -> 1-centered" - the standard folds trait words onto layouts too, and that arrow claimed the two were the same thing; now gated on is_layout_id(). (2) The no-change rows in the collapse table were painted with --tint (3.5% black) and then --wash (8%), both of which composited to within a couple of values of the page ground - the caption promising a shaded row was a lie. Now the accent at 14%, the same colour the 1920 bars use.

DECISION CHANGED: best.md is served by route() on the patterns page, not by core Page's "a .md beside me IS a page" fallback. The fallback only fires AFTER a probe for best/page.js 404s, and that 404 lands in every readers console (measured: 1 on /websites/patterns/best/, 0 after the switch). /websites/doc/ moved to route() for the same reason.

assign.outcome:
**What the web mostly does, counted live — and the best of each kind, judged from the shots.**

One new page, [`/websites/patterns/`](/websites/patterns/), whose every number is counted at render from `site/index.json`. Nothing on it is typed: add a site, re-run `tools/index.mjs`, and the headline, the bars and the table all move by themselves.

![the patterns page at 1920](patterns-1920.jpg)

**The sentence it renders:** *Of 47 real websites, 21 are one column at 1920, 16 are two, 8 are three and 2 are four. At 400 all but 9 are `1-flow` — and 7 of those 9 are still a single column, so only 2 of the 47 keep a second column on a phone.* My own Node count over the index agrees exactly.

- **The most common whole-page layout at 1920 is [`2-sidebar`](/websites/tag/2-sidebar/), 14 of 47** — and all 14 become `1-flow` at 400, the most predictable collapse in the corpus. At 400 the winner is `1-flow`, 38 of 47.
- **[The best of each kind →](/websites/patterns/best/)** — one site per category, written after opening its own 3440 and 400 shots: Wikipedia, Stripe, the NYT, Josh Comeau, GitHub, Allbirds, Shopify Polaris, CcType. Then three layouts to copy (`2-sidebar`, `1-centered`, `n-wall`) and three to avoid (`4-1`, `1-flow` as a desktop page, `3-holy-grail` with no ceiling on its middle).
- **Registered where readers already are:** `patterns` is in [`/websites/`](/websites/)'s `children:` and on its front ("What emerged →"), and [`/layouts/`](/layouts/) now points here too.
- **Docs:** [the readme](/websites/patterns/readme.md) — the index, plus the two traps this page walked into.

**Two defects found by looking and fixed.** The alias arrow fired on tags as well as ids, so the tag panel read `measure → 1-centered` and claimed a trait word was a layout. And the no-change rows in the collapse table were painted `--tint` and then `--wash`, both of which composited to within a couple of values of the page ground — the caption promising a shaded row was a lie. They wear the accent at 14% now.

**Verified:** 400, 1600 and 1920 headless — zero console errors, zero 4xx, no horizontal overflow, nothing at x:0, no unwanted scrollers; all 8 inline shots on `best/` load and all 42 of its links resolve against `layouts.json` and `site/index.json`.

**Left deliberately.** The corpus spells its documentation category three ways (`documentation` 5, `docs` 2, `reference` 1) and still writes two retired layout spellings (`3-cards`, `4-equal`); the page counts what the records say and `best.md` judges the three doc spellings as one. Fixing the records is a corpus job and my fence forbade writing one. No `patterns/doc/` dir: the module's docs live at [`/websites/doc/`](/websites/doc/) and this page's two decisions fit in its readme. The usage snapshot was not refreshed — `ai/usage.json` is outside my write fence.
